items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1979-03-26
items.q: Snoozer Quinn, of course, was a big friend of mine.

ctx.x: His name was, uh, Jack Bunch. And he was with the band that Woody Herman started with in New Orleans at Club Forest in 1932. It was called Tom Guerinovich. Yeah. Later shortened to Tom Guerin. And his band, they were from San Francisco. Very popular in New Orleans. And, uh, anybody who played at Club Forest was popular, I'll tell you that. Ben Pollock played there. Yeah. And, uh, I visited Jack there. Snoozer Quinn, of course, was a big friend of mine. He was in New Orleans at the time. But, uh, tricks were all…
Who did Ezell play with in New York?

items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1978-12-03
items.q: Snoozer used to come down and play for me.

ctx.x: What was the name of the restaurant?

I can't remember, but it was just almost directly across the street. It was in the 327, close to where the Royal Semester is now. And I lived at the Pontaubo building as soon as I got a salary, and had another close friend at Royal Arms who was in the refrigerator department, the name was Bennett D's. And then I shared 519, we lived at 519 St. Henn, first floor apartment, $45 a month. He paid $22.50 and I paid $22.50. And he was a great bathtub gin mixer, and we had lots of fun. Snoozer used to come down and play…
Well, I have a few little questions. I'd be glad if you would. Okay. Uh, we covered a lot of territory. Uh, what kind of reeds did Fahs use? You were talking about something? Vandora.
